title: Variable Scope
objectives: Tell local and global variables apart
Understand that an assignment inside a function does not affect an outer variable with the same name

hook.text: You wrote "x ← 20" inside a function. Does the x outside the function still keep its old value, or did it change?

concept.heading: Global and local variables
concept.body: A global variable can be seen from everywhere in the program. A local variable exists only inside the function where it was DEFINED, and it disappears when the function ends. A function's parameters are local too.

captions: the function is running: local y = 5
the function ended → y is gone

concept.heading: Why doesn't an assignment inside a function affect the outside?
concept.body: When you assign a value to a variable inside a function (even if there is a global with the same name), this creates a NEW local variable and does NOT TOUCH the outer global. A function can READ a global variable, but if it writes to it (makes an assignment), it creates its own local copy.

captions: in the function x ← 99 → a NEW local x

workedExamples.prompt: Make an assignment to a variable with the same name inside a function. Does the outer variable change?
workedExamples.runnerSource:
x ← 10
FUNCTION change()
  x ← 20
END
result ← change()
WRITE x

steps.explain: Inside the function, x ← 20 runs, but this is a LOCAL x and does not touch the global x.
After the function ends and the local x is gone, WRITE x prints the global x (10).

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: The 'number ← number * 2' inside the function creates a new local number, NOT the outer global number.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: A function can READ a global variable (factor) that it did not define.

exercises.question: What scope are a function's parameters in?

feedback.correct: Correct. Parameters are local variables that exist only inside that function call.
feedback.incorrect: Parameters are local: they exist only for the duration of the function call where they are defined.

exercises.question: Can a function reach a global variable that it did not define (it only reads it)?
options: Only if it is a CONST
Only if it is a parameter

feedback.correct: Correct. Functions can read global variables that they do not assign to themselves.
feedback.incorrect: A function can read global variables as long as it has not created its own local copy.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: A variable that exists only inside the function where it was defined is called a ___ variable.

exercises.question: What is the best answer to the question "Why are local variables useful?"
options: Changes inside a function do not accidentally break the rest of the program

feedback.correct: Correct. Local variables prevent side effects by isolating functions from each other and from the global code.
feedback.incorrect: The biggest benefit of local variables is that changes inside a function do not accidentally affect the outside.

summary: Global variable: visible everywhere. Local variable: exists only inside the function where it was defined.
Assigning to a variable inside a function creates a NEW local variable, even if a global with the same name exists.
A function can read global variables that it does not assign to itself.
